meta.title: UK tax identity framework
meta.purpose: Explain how legal existence, tax treatment, residence, activity, control, reporting and filing identity can point to different subjects at the same time.
meta.portability: The dimensions are jurisdiction-portable. The classifications, examples and legal conclusions in this release are UK-first and must not be copied to another jurisdiction without local sources.
meta.warning: Educational public reference only. It is not legal advice, an authority determination, a filing position or a substitute for the exact law and facts for the tax, place and period in question.

It does not relicense legislation, official guidance, model standards, linked source text, trademarks or other third-party material; each source keeps its own rights and reuse terms.

editorialRules: Never collapse legal form, taxable person, reporting person and beneficial owner into one label.
Every assertion states subjectRef, jurisdiction, taxOrRegime, activityOrContext, ruleset, status and an effective-date basis.
Treat identifiers and registrations as evidence, not as proof of the underlying classification.
Keep unknown, conditional, disputed and not-applicable distinct.
Model a branch, permanent establishment or VAT fixed establishment as a nexus overlay unless local law creates a separate legal person.
A model convention or international standard is not enacted domestic law or the text of an actual treaty.
A change creates a new effective-dated assertion; it does not rewrite the earlier one.
Every classification is individually sourced, its source IDs are included in the parent dimension source list, and every synthetic subject is used by at least one assertion.
boundaries: No names, tax identifiers, addresses, ownership records or private taxpayer facts.
No endpoint accepts a person's or organisation's facts in this release.
No eligibility, liability, residence, employment-status, beneficial-owner or permanent-establishment decision.
No filing, payment, registration, authority contact or external state change.
No numerical confidence score; gaps and review triggers are stated in words.

sources.title: Partnership Act 1890, section 1
supports: The statutory partnership definition is a relationship between persons carrying on business in common with a view of profit.
The 1890 Act declared and amended an existing field of partnership law rather than inventing every partnership relationship.
limitations: Legal personality differs within the UK and tax statutes can apply a different treatment.

sources.title: Partnership Act 1890, section 4
supports: A Scottish firm is a legal person distinct from its partners.
limitations: Separate Scottish legal personality does not by itself decide the treatment under a particular tax.

sources.title: Companies Act 2006, section 16
supports: Registration forms a body corporate capable of exercising the functions of an incorporated company.
limitations: Corporate existence does not settle residence, beneficial ownership, VAT grouping or foreign tax classification.

sources.title: Limited Liability Partnerships Act 2000, section 1
sources.jurisdiction: Great Britain at creation; later extended to Northern Ireland
supports: The Act created the Great Britain LLP form as a body corporate with legal personality separate from its members.
The current territorial position cannot be read from the original 2000 creation event alone.
limitations: The Act's general-law personality does not make an LLP a company taxpayer for every tax.
Northern Ireland first used separate 2002 legislation; Companies Act 2006 section 1286 later extended the Great Britain enactments and ended the separate Act.

sources.title: Limited Liability Partnerships Act (Northern Ireland) 2002, section 1
supports: Northern Ireland created its own LLP form as a body corporate with legal personality separate from its members.
limitations: This is an origin source, not current standalone law: Companies Act 2006 section 1286 later provided that the Act ceased to have effect.

sources.title: Companies Act 2006, section 1286
supports: The Great Britain enactments relating to limited liability partnerships extend to Northern Ireland.
The separate Limited Liability Partnerships Act (Northern Ireland) 2002 ceased to have effect accordingly.
limitations: Formation date, commencement and transitional provisions still matter for a point-in-time conclusion.

sources.title: PM120100: What is a partnership?
supports: A partnership is a relationship and can include natural or artificial persons.
English, Welsh and Northern Irish partnerships lack separate legal personality while Scottish partnerships have it.
A partnership can still be a person for Taxes Acts purposes.
limitations: HMRC manuals explain HMRC's view and are not themselves legislation.

sources.title: PM131450: LLP taxation
supports: An LLP carrying on business with a view to profit is normally treated as a partnership for income and gains.
Members are generally charged on their shares even though the LLP is a body corporate.
The salaried-members rules can add employment treatment for PAYE and Class 1 National Insurance purposes without changing a member's chargeable profit share.
limitations: Partnership treatment still depends on the activity, period and exact tax provision; salaried-member treatment is a separate member-level payroll and National Insurance overlay.

sources.title: PM136000: Taxing partnership profits
supports: Partnership business profits are computed at partnership level and attributed to partners.
The partnership can still carry PAYE and VAT responsibilities.
limitations: Transparent and opaque are shorthand; charge-specific rules still control.

sources.title: INTM180010: Foreign entity classification
supports: Transparent and opaque are informal labels for who is liable on what income or gains.
The exact UK tax provision must be considered rather than applying one entity-wide label.
limitations: A general HMRC view can vary after examining a specific foreign entity's constitution and facts.

sources.title: INTM120040: Company residence incorporation rule
supports: Subject to stated exceptions, a UK-incorporated company is UK resident for corporation tax.
limitations: Treaty rules and the full statutory exceptions must be checked.

sources.title: INTM120180: Reviewing company residence
supports: Central management and control is a factual inquiry informed by the governing law and constitution.
limitations: Meeting location alone is not conclusive.

sources.title: RDRM20060: Domicile background and the 2025 change
supports: From 6 April 2025, domicile as a relevant tax connecting factor was replaced by a residence-based system in the scope described by HMRC.
Nationality, residence and domicile are distinct concepts.
limitations: Historical periods and taxes outside the changed regime require their own rules.

sources.title: TSEM1563: Bare trusts
supports: A bare-trust beneficiary with immediate and absolute title is strictly chargeable on the trust income and gains.
Trustees can act administratively without becoming the person strictly charged.
limitations: Whether a trust is bare depends on its terms and facts and can require legal advice.

sources.title: TSEM10020: Trustees as a single person and trustee residence
supports: For Income Tax and Capital Gains Tax, trustees of a settlement are treated as a single deemed person distinct from the actual trustees.
The trustee-residence rules and their effective dates must be applied to the settlement and period in question.
limitations: The deemed-person rule is tax-specific and does not turn the trust arrangement into a general-law legal person.

sources.title: TSEM4200: Settlor-interested settlements
supports: Some settlement income can be treated as the settlor's income.
limitations: The detailed statutory conditions and exceptions control.

sources.title: Finance Act 2010, Part 1
supports: Tax law defines charity, charitable company and charitable trust for the taxes within its scope.
limitations: Charity-law registration and tax recognition are related but not identical classifications.

sources.title: Tax exemptions for charities
supports: Charitable-company and charitable-trust exemptions arise under different tax provisions.
Relief is conditional, including on application of income to charitable purposes.
limitations: Charity status is not a blanket exemption from every tax or activity.

sources.title: Group and divisional registration, VAT Notice 700/2
supports: Eligible persons can be treated as one taxable person for VAT.
The representative member files and pays for the group while members can remain jointly and severally liable.
Group members keep their separate legal existence.
limitations: Eligibility, establishment, control and anti-avoidance conditions must be checked.

sources.title: VATREG08750: Registration of partnerships
supports: Partners acting collectively can be treated as a person for VAT even where the firm lacks separate legal personality.
A person acting alone and the same person acting with others in partnership can be different VAT persons.
limitations: Scottish partnerships and changes in partner composition require separate treatment.

sources.title: INTM162060: Branches, permanent establishments and residence certificates
supports: A branch or permanent establishment of a non-resident is not a separate legal person resident in the UK.
The non-resident can still be taxed on income attributable to the UK presence.
limitations: The existence and profit attribution of a permanent establishment are separate technical questions.

sources.title: OECD Model Tax Convention 2017
supports: Person, residence and permanent establishment are separate treaty concepts.
A permanent establishment is generally a fixed place through which an enterprise's business is carried on.
Treaty treatment of transparent entities depends on how income is treated under relevant domestic law.
limitations: The applicable bilateral treaty and its current protocol control, not the model alone.

sources.title: Preventing the Artificial Avoidance of Permanent Establishment Status, Action 7 final report
supports: The 2015 final report proposed treaty changes addressing commissionnaire and similar arrangements, preparatory or auxiliary exceptions, fragmentation and contract splitting.
The work changed the model-standard PE lineage rather than itself creating a UK PE in a private case.
limitations: The actual treaty, multilateral-instrument position, domestic law, effective date and facts control.

sources.title: Consolidated text of the Common Reporting Standard 2025
supports: CRS Entity, Financial Institution, Active NFE, Passive NFE and Controlling Person are separate reporting classifications.
A trust's controlling-person roles include settlors, trustees, protectors, beneficiaries or classes and other persons exercising ultimate effective control.
limitations: Domestic implementation and effective dates control reporting obligations.
The 2025 consolidation includes amendments whose first exchanges are expected later.

sources.title: Guidance on Beneficial Ownership of Legal Persons
supports: Beneficial owners are natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal person.
Legal ownership and ultimate beneficial ownership can differ.
Accurate, adequate and up-to-date information needs more than one source.
limitations: FATF standards require domestic implementation and do not decide a person's tax liability.

sources.title: Guidance on Beneficial Ownership and Transparency of Legal Arrangements
supports: A trust is a legal arrangement governing relationships between parties rather than necessarily a legal person.
Trust roles and ultimate effective control must be kept distinct.
limitations: The governing law and domestic implementation remain decisive.

sources.title: Council Directive 2006/112/EC, Articles 9 and 10
supports: VAT taxable-person status turns on independently carrying on economic activity.
An employee can be outside that independent capacity while having another capacity elsewhere.
limitations: Member-state implementation and post-exit UK VAT law must be checked for the relevant period.

sources.title: Council Implementing Regulation 282/2011, Article 11
supports: A VAT fixed establishment requires sufficient permanence and suitable human and technical resources for the rule in question.
A VAT identification number alone is insufficient.
limitations: Different VAT provisions use the definition for different functions.
For a current UK conclusion, check UK VAT law and HMRC's current manuals; this EU instrument is retained here as lineage and comparison.

sources.title: Employment status: self-employed and contractor
supports: One person can be employed and self-employed at the same time.
Employment status for tax is checked for the particular working relationship and can differ from employment-law status.
limitations: The page is general guidance and does not determine a real engagement.

sources.title: PAYE and payroll for employers
supports: An employer normally operates PAYE through payroll to collect Income Tax and National Insurance from employment.
The employer deducts, reports and pays under the payroll rules rather than becoming the employee's income-tax taxpayer.
limitations: Registration thresholds, worker status, special cases and the rules for the period still need separate checks.

sources.title: VAT guide, Notice 700
supports: Current UK VAT guidance keeps business and non-business activities separate.
A VAT business is a continuing activity mainly concerned with making supplies to other persons for consideration, with frequency and scale.
limitations: General guidance does not replace the VAT Act, detailed manuals or transaction-specific rules.

sources.title: VATPOSS04500: fixed establishment
supports: HMRC's current UK view looks for sufficient permanence and human and technical resources for making or receiving the supplies in question.
A registered office or identifier does not by itself settle the fixed-establishment question.
limitations: The conclusion is provision-specific and fact-specific, and relevant case law and current legislation must also be checked.

sources.title: Classification of taxpayers for US tax purposes
supports: Eligible entities can have a federal tax classification different from their state-law form.
A single-owner eligible entity can be disregarded or elect association treatment.
limitations: Disregarded treatment has charge-specific exceptions and does not determine UK treatment.

sources.title: Treasury Decision 8697
supports: The check-the-box entity-classification regulations generally became applicable in 1997.
limitations: Later amendments and the current Code and regulations must be checked.

sources.title: Help with sharing group structure information
supports: A UK company can be a company where incorporated and disregarded for US tax.
A UK LLP can be transparent in the UK and treated as a corporation elsewhere.
Incorporation and tax residence belong on separate parts of a group map.
limitations: Diagram notation communicates claims; it does not prove them.

sources.title: How to set up as a sole trader
supports: A sole trader and the business are not separate legal persons.
A trading name does not create a separate person.
limitations: Tax obligations still depend on activities, income, registrations and period.

dimensions.label: Legal existence and form
dimensions.question: What exists under the governing private law?
dimensions.meaning: Start with the natural person, body, relationship or arrangement created by general law. This is the legal shell, not the whole tax answer.
dimensions.origin: Company, partnership, trust and association law creates or recognises these categories. Tax law can borrow, override or ignore them for a stated purpose.

classificationValues.label: Natural person
classificationValues.meaning: A human legal person.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: One unchanging tax capacity or one source of income.

classificationValues.label: Body corporate
classificationValues.meaning: A separate incorporated legal person.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Opaque or company-taxed in every jurisdiction and charge.

classificationValues.label: Unincorporated relationship
classificationValues.meaning: A relationship such as an English general partnership, without separate general-law personality.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Invisible to tax administration or incapable of filing.

classificationValues.label: Separate firm person
classificationValues.meaning: A firm with distinct legal personality, such as a Scottish partnership.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Entity-level taxation of its business profits.

classificationValues.label: Legal arrangement
classificationValues.meaning: A relationship governing property and roles, such as a trust.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: One universal trust taxpayer.

classificationValues.label: Non-separate presence
classificationValues.meaning: A branch or business presence that is part of another person.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: No local taxing nexus.

classificationValues.label: Tax group, not a new legal person
classificationValues.meaning: A grouping that a tax regime treats together.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The member entities disappear for other law or taxes.

reviewWhen: The subject is formed outside the jurisdiction applying the tax.
The governing documents or formation status are unavailable.
A partnership is connected with Scotland.
A label such as company, foundation, association or trust has been translated from another legal system.

dimensions.label: Tax attribution and charge
dimensions.question: For this tax and item, who is treated as earning, owning or disposing?
dimensions.meaning: Tax can charge the legal person, look through to members, attribute to a beneficiary or settlor, or use a representative member.
dimensions.origin: Each charging provision defines or implies its own taxpayer and attribution rule. Transparent and opaque are convenient descriptions, not universal properties.

classificationValues.label: Scoped subject charge
classificationValues.meaning: The scoped natural person or legal entity is charged on the relevant item in its own name.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The subject has one treatment for every item, or that owners have no separate distribution, gain, payroll or reporting consequences.

classificationValues.label: Member-level attribution
classificationValues.meaning: Members or partners are charged on attributed shares.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The partnership has no computation, return, VAT or PAYE role.

classificationValues.label: Owner-level attribution
classificationValues.meaning: The stated regime looks through a separate legal form and charges its owner on the relevant item.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The legal entity disappears, another jurisdiction follows the look-through, or every tax uses the same treatment.

classificationValues.label: Beneficiary-level attribution
classificationValues.meaning: The beneficiary is charged on the relevant trust income or gains.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Every trust is bare or every trust item follows this rule.

classificationValues.label: Trustee-level charge
classificationValues.meaning: Trustees are the persons charged or assessed for the stated rule.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Trustees beneficially own the property.

classificationValues.label: Settlor attribution
classificationValues.meaning: A settlement rule attributes the item to the settlor.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The settlor is always charged on trust income.

classificationValues.label: Single VAT taxable person
classificationValues.meaning: Several members are treated together for VAT through a representative member.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: One company for corporation tax or company law.

classificationValues.label: Main entity with attributed presence
classificationValues.meaning: The main person remains the taxpayer while profits are attributed to a branch or permanent establishment.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The presence is a separate resident legal person.

reviewWhen: A transparent or opaque label is being reused across taxes.
An LLP is not carrying on a business with a view to profit or is winding up.
A trust type or entitlement is unclear.
Two jurisdictions classify the same body differently.

dimensions.label: Capacity and activity
dimensions.question: In what role is the subject acting for this item or engagement?
dimensions.meaning: The same person can be an employee, sole trader, landlord, partner, trustee, director, employer and investor at the same time.
dimensions.origin: Charging rules and case law classify an activity or relationship, not a whole human being for all purposes.

classificationValues.label: Employee
classificationValues.meaning: Acting under an employment relationship for the stated engagement.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Unable to carry on a separate trade.

classificationValues.label: Sole trader
classificationValues.meaning: A natural person carrying on business on their own account.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: A separate legal person called the business.

classificationValues.label: Partner or LLP member
classificationValues.meaning: Acting as a participant in the partnership business.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Employment or self-employment status is settled for every rule.

classificationValues.label: Salaried LLP member for tax and National Insurance
classificationValues.meaning: An individual LLP member meeting all salaried-member conditions is treated like an employee for the reward, PAYE and Class 1 National Insurance rules.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The member stops being a member or their chargeable share of LLP profits changes.

classificationValues.label: Company carrying on activity
classificationValues.meaning: The body corporate carries on the stated trade or business.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Every receipt belongs to the trade or every director acts personally.

classificationValues.label: Charitable capacity
classificationValues.meaning: The subject is recognised and acts for charitable purposes within the stated rule.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: All activities and income are exempt.

classificationValues.label: Trustee
classificationValues.meaning: Holding or administering property under trust duties.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Beneficial ownership.

classificationValues.label: Beneficiary
classificationValues.meaning: Holding a beneficial interest or entitlement.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Control, legal title or present tax liability in every trust.

classificationValues.label: Independent economic actor
classificationValues.meaning: Independently carrying on economic activity for the VAT rule.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Self-employed for every direct-tax or employment-law rule.

reviewWhen: One person has more than one income source or engagement.
Employment and self-employment labels are inferred from a job title.
A director's personal and company capacities are mixed.
A charity carries on trading or investment activity.

dimensions.label: Residence and territorial nexus
dimensions.question: Which place claims residence, source or another taxing foothold for this regime?
dimensions.meaning: Incorporation, residence, domicile, source, permanent establishment, VAT fixed establishment and payroll presence are different connecting tests.
dimensions.origin: Domestic law first makes residence and source claims; treaties coordinate only their own application; indirect-tax and payroll rules use separate connections.

classificationValues.label: UK domestic resident
classificationValues.meaning: UK domestic law treats the subject as resident for the stated tax and period.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Exclusive treaty residence or residence for every reporting regime.

classificationValues.label: Dual domestic residence
classificationValues.meaning: More than one jurisdiction's domestic law treats the subject as resident.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The conflict has been resolved for treaty purposes.

classificationValues.label: Treaty-coordinated residence
classificationValues.meaning: An applicable treaty coordinates residence for that treaty.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The domestic residence claims cease to exist for all law.

classificationValues.label: Permanent establishment
classificationValues.meaning: A direct-tax business presence meeting the relevant domestic or treaty test.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Subsidiary, registered branch, VAT fixed establishment or separate legal person.

classificationValues.label: VAT fixed establishment
classificationValues.meaning: A VAT presence with the required permanence and human and technical resources for the rule.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: A VAT number alone or a direct-tax permanent establishment.

classificationValues.label: No separate residence
classificationValues.meaning: The branch, group or arrangement has no independent residence claim in the stated context.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: No local tax or reporting obligation.

reviewWhen: Management, board or controlling decisions cross borders.
A remote worker, agent, office or technical resource is in another jurisdiction.
A certificate, address or VAT number is being treated as conclusive.
The actual bilateral treaty and protocol have not been read.
The period crosses a legal change, including 6 April 2025.

dimensions.label: Registration, election and grouping
dimensions.question: Which administrative accounts, elections or tax groups apply?
dimensions.meaning: Registration and elections can create obligations or tax-specific treatment, but a number in a database is not the underlying legal conclusion.
dimensions.origin: Company, charity and revenue registries, statutory elections and grouping rules create purpose-specific administrative identities.

classificationValues.label: Companies House registration
classificationValues.meaning: The incorporated form is recorded by the company registrar.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Tax residence, activity or beneficial ownership is proved.

classificationValues.label: Self Assessment record
classificationValues.meaning: A person or filing unit has a UK Self Assessment administration record.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Every recorded source is current or correctly classified.

classificationValues.label: Charity and tax recognition
classificationValues.meaning: Charity-law registration or recognition and HMRC tax recognition have been addressed.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: One registration necessarily supplies the other.

classificationValues.label: VAT registration
classificationValues.meaning: The stated taxable person is registered or required to register.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Every cost is business input tax or a fixed establishment exists.

classificationValues.label: VAT group membership
classificationValues.meaning: Eligible members are treated through one representative registration.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Corporate or direct-tax consolidation.

classificationValues.label: Payroll registration
classificationValues.meaning: An employer or payer operates a payroll reporting account.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The same subject is the income-tax taxpayer on every profit.

classificationValues.label: Classification election
classificationValues.meaning: An available election changes a tax classification from an effective date.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The legal form changes or another jurisdiction follows the election.

classificationValues.label: No registration is determinative
classificationValues.meaning: The current evidence contains no registration that settles the classification.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: No registration duty exists.

reviewWhen: A legal conclusion is inferred from a UTR, VRN, EIN, TIN, company number or address.
An election date or acceptance is missing.
Group membership changed during the period.
The registered person differs from the person economically active.

dimensions.label: Ownership, control and benefit
dimensions.question: Who holds legal title, benefits, exercises formal power or has ultimate effective control?
dimensions.meaning: Shareholder, member, legal owner, beneficial owner, trustee, beneficiary and controlling person are related roles, not synonyms.
dimensions.origin: Property and company law allocate title and formal power; anti-money-laundering and reporting rules look through to natural persons and other means of control.

classificationValues.label: Legal owner
classificationValues.meaning: Holds legal title to the interest or property.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Ultimate benefit or effective control.

classificationValues.label: Beneficial owner
classificationValues.meaning: The natural person who ultimately owns or benefits within the stated standard.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The direct registered holder.

classificationValues.label: Member or partner
classificationValues.meaning: Participates in the body or relationship under its governing rules.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Employee, beneficial owner or controlling person in every case.

classificationValues.label: Trustee legal title
classificationValues.meaning: Trustees hold or administer legal title under trust duties.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The trustees own for their personal benefit.

classificationValues.label: Beneficiary interest
classificationValues.meaning: A person or class has a beneficial interest or entitlement.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Present control or a presently taxable receipt.

classificationValues.label: Common control
classificationValues.meaning: Members satisfy a tax regime's control connection.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: All activities or liabilities merge.

classificationValues.label: CRS controlling person
classificationValues.meaning: A natural person falls within the reporting standard's controlling-person analysis.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: They are automatically the taxpayer or guilty of wrongdoing.

reviewWhen: Nominees, trusts, indirect chains or non-share control are present.
The registered holder is assumed to be the ultimate owner.
A senior managing official is treated as a beneficial owner without stating the fallback rule.
Private ownership information would be exposed.

dimensions.label: Reporting classification
dimensions.question: How does the relevant reporting or due-diligence regime classify the subject?
dimensions.meaning: CRS, FATCA and other information regimes create their own entity and controlling-person buckets.
dimensions.origin: International reporting standards and their domestic implementation define purpose-specific classes distinct from income-tax treatment.

classificationValues.label: Individual account holder or reportable person
classificationValues.meaning: The reporting regime treats the subject as an individual.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: No business capacity.

classificationValues.label: Financial Institution
classificationValues.meaning: The subject meets the reporting standard's financial-institution definition.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: A bank in ordinary speech.

classificationValues.label: Active NFE
classificationValues.meaning: The entity meets one of the reporting standard's active non-financial entity tests.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Active trading for every tax.

classificationValues.label: Passive NFE
classificationValues.meaning: The entity falls within the reporting standard's passive category.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Tax avoidance or illegality.

classificationValues.label: Trust role reporting
classificationValues.meaning: Settlor, trustee, protector, beneficiary and other control roles are analysed for reporting.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Every role has the same ownership, control or tax consequence.

classificationValues.label: Members remain separately classified
classificationValues.meaning: A tax group does not replace each member's reporting classification.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Group membership is irrelevant to every report.

reviewWhen: Income and asset tests are missing.
A tax-transparent label is reused as a CRS classification.
A dual-resident entity has been reduced to one country without checking the amended standard and domestic implementation.
A reporting result is treated as an income-tax conclusion.

dimensions.label: Filing, payment and withholding role
dimensions.question: Who must calculate, return, pay, withhold or report?
dimensions.meaning: The person who files or remits can differ from the person on whom the underlying income or gain is charged.
dimensions.origin: Administrative and collection rules assign practical duties to taxpayers, partnerships, trustees, employers, agents and representative members.

classificationValues.label: Taxpayer and filer
classificationValues.meaning: The same subject is charged and files for the stated obligation.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: No agent, withholding or group role.

classificationValues.label: Filing unit, members charged
classificationValues.meaning: The relationship computes or reports while members bear the underlying charge.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The filing unit is irrelevant.

classificationValues.label: Representative member
classificationValues.meaning: One member accounts for the group under the tax regime.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Other members lose all liability.

classificationValues.label: Employer or withholding role
classificationValues.meaning: The subject deducts, reports or pays amounts connected with another person's income.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The employer is the employee's income-tax taxpayer.

classificationValues.label: Trustee administration
classificationValues.meaning: Trustees return, account or pay in an administrative capacity for the stated rule.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: Trustees are always the person strictly chargeable.

classificationValues.label: Main entity with PE return
classificationValues.meaning: The non-resident person reports and pays on profits attributed to its local presence.
classificationValues.doesNotMean: The PE is a separately resident company.

reviewWhen: A filing name is treated as proof of who bears the charge.
Partners, trustees, employers or VAT-group members share or divide duties.
A branch or agent submits on behalf of a non-resident.
Joint and several liability is possible.

archetypes.label: UK sole trader
archetypes.summary: One natural person carries on a business; the trading name does not become a second legal person.

taxRoles.subject: The natural person
taxRoles.caveat: The trade is a separate income source but not a separate legal person.

taxRoles.subject: The natural person acting as taxable person
taxRoles.caveat: All business activities of that registered person normally sit under the registration; business purpose remains item-specific.

commonMisreadings: Treating a business name as a company.
Assuming employee and sole-trader capacities cannot coexist.
Treating a UTR or VAT number as proof of employment status.

archetypes.label: English, Welsh or Northern Irish general partnership
archetypes.summary: The partnership relationship lacks separate general-law personality, yet tax law can treat the firm as a filing or VAT person while attributing business profits to partners.

taxRoles.taxOrRegime: Income or Corporation Tax on partnership profits
taxRoles.subject: The partners
taxRoles.caveat: The partnership computes and returns the business result.

taxRoles.subject: The partners acting collectively
taxRoles.caveat: A change in partners can change the VAT person.

commonMisreadings: Calling the firm legally invisible because it files.
Calling the firm a separate company because it has a UTR or VRN.
Assuming the same partner set after a membership change.

archetypes.label: Scottish general partnership
archetypes.summary: The firm has separate legal personality, while business profits can still be attributed to partners under UK tax rules.

taxRoles.taxOrRegime: Income or Corporation Tax on partnership profits
taxRoles.subject: The partners
taxRoles.caveat: Separate Scots-law personality does not force entity-level taxation.

commonMisreadings: Applying the English legal-personality answer across the UK.
Assuming separate personality means opaque taxation.

archetypes.label: Great Britain limited liability partnership
archetypes.summary: The Great Britain LLP form created by the 2000 Act is a separate body corporate in general law but is normally treated like a partnership for income and gains when it carries on business with a view to profit.

taxRoles.subject: The members
taxRoles.caveat: Business-with-a-view-to-profit and winding-up exceptions need separate checks.

taxRoles.subject: An individual member meeting all salaried-member conditions
taxRoles.role: Employment-treatment overlay for the member's reward
taxRoles.caveat: The overlay does not change the amount of that member's chargeable share of LLP profits.

taxRoles.subject: The LLP
taxRoles.role: Registered body filing accounts and notices
taxRoles.caveat: A company-law filing role does not make it a company for the partnership tax provisions.

commonMisreadings: Treating body corporate and company taxpayer as synonyms.
Calling LLP transparency unconditional.
Assuming every LLP member has the same employment or National Insurance status.

archetypes.label: Northern Ireland limited liability partnership lineage
archetypes.summary: Northern Ireland created a separate LLP form in 2002; Companies Act 2006 section 1286 later extended the Great Britain enactments to Northern Ireland and ended the separate Act.

taxRoles.subject: The Northern Ireland LLP
taxRoles.role: Body corporate under the legislation effective for its period

archetypes.label: UK private limited company
archetypes.summary: The company is a body corporate separate from shareholders and directors, with tax residence and activity tested on their own dimensions.

taxRoles.subject: The company
taxRoles.role: Taxpayer on its profits and gains
taxRoles.caveat: Residence, source, group rules and distributions can create further classifications.

commonMisreadings: Treating director, shareholder and company as one taxpayer.
Treating registered office as proof of actual management.
Assuming another jurisdiction follows the UK classification.

archetypes.label: UK charitable company
archetypes.summary: One body can simultaneously be a company, a charity and an employer, with tax reliefs conditional on the income, activity and use of funds.

taxRoles.subject: The charitable company
taxRoles.caveat: Trading, property, gains and application to charitable purposes must be tested under the relevant provision.

commonMisreadings: Treating charity as a base legal form.
Treating recognition as a blanket tax exemption.
Treating members, trustees or directors as beneficial owners of charitable assets.

archetypes.label: UK express trust
archetypes.summary: A trust is a legal arrangement with settlor, trustee, beneficiary and possible protector roles; the person charged can change with the trust type and rule.

taxRoles.subject: The beneficiary
taxRoles.role: Strictly chargeable where immediate and absolute entitlement exists
taxRoles.caveat: Whether the trust is bare is a legal and factual question.

taxRoles.subject: Trustees, settlor or beneficiaries depending on the rule
taxRoles.role: Charge and administration divided by statute
taxRoles.caveat: No generic trust-taxpayer answer is safe.

commonMisreadings: Calling the trust itself a company-like legal person.
Treating legal title, beneficial interest and control as one role.
Assuming the person filing is the person strictly chargeable.

archetypes.label: UK VAT group
archetypes.summary: Several eligible persons retain their legal identities while VAT treats the group through one representative member as a single taxable person.

taxRoles.subject: The grouped taxable person through its representative member
taxRoles.caveat: Members can remain jointly and severally liable.

taxRoles.subject: Each member company
taxRoles.caveat: VAT grouping does not merge them for other purposes.

commonMisreadings: Calling the VAT group a new company.
Using one VAT number as proof of one beneficial owner or one corporation-tax payer.
Forgetting effective dates when membership changes.

archetypes.label: Foreign company with a UK branch or permanent establishment
archetypes.summary: The foreign company remains the legal person, while a UK presence can create a local charge and profit-attribution exercise.

taxRoles.taxOrRegime: Corporation Tax on UK permanent-establishment profits
taxRoles.subject: The non-resident company
taxRoles.caveat: The existence of the PE and the amount attributable to it are separate questions.

commonMisreadings: Treating branch, subsidiary, PE and VAT fixed establishment as synonyms.
Issuing residence conclusions in the branch's name.
Assuming a registered branch proves a PE or vice versa.

overlaps.label: One person, personal and business capacities
overlaps.meaning: There is one legal person, but transactions and expenses still have to be assigned to the correct personal, employment, trading or other capacity.
overlaps.dangerousShortcut: Creating a fictional second person called the business, or treating every personal item as a business item.
questions: Which activity produced the item?
Was the person acting independently or under an employment relationship?
Which registration covers the activity?
reviewTriggers: Mixed employment and self-employment.
Shared personal and business assets or expenses.
More than one trade or partnership role.

overlaps.label: Separate body corporate, member-level taxation
overlaps.meaning: The LLP owns, contracts and files as a body corporate while the relevant income and gains are normally attributed to members.
overlaps.dangerousShortcut: Calling the LLP a company taxpayer because it is incorporated, or calling it legally unincorporated because it is transparent.
questions: Is it carrying on a business with a view to profit?
Which tax and item are being classified?
Do the salaried-member or winding-up exceptions matter?
reviewTriggers: Non-profit activity, winding up or temporary cessation.
A member may fall within salaried-members rules.
Another jurisdiction classifies the LLP.

overlaps.label: Separate Scottish firm, member-level taxation
overlaps.meaning: Scots law can recognise the firm as a person while UK partnership tax still looks through to partners.
overlaps.dangerousShortcut: Applying either the English legal answer or an entity-level tax answer merely because the firm is a person.
questions: Which UK law territory governs the firm?
Which charge and filing duty are in view?
reviewTriggers: The place of formation or governing law is unclear.
The structure includes limited partnerships or cross-border partners.

overlaps.label: Company form and charity status
overlaps.meaning: The company remains a company taxpayer while charity status can provide conditional reliefs for qualifying income and use.
overlaps.dangerousShortcut: Replacing the legal form with charity, or replacing a conditional exemption with tax-free.
questions: Which legal form does the charity use?
Is the income from a qualifying activity?
Is the income or gain applied to charitable purposes?
reviewTriggers: Non-primary-purpose trading.
Mixed charitable and non-charitable expenditure.
Registration and HMRC recognition do not align.

overlaps.label: Separate companies, one VAT taxable person
overlaps.meaning: VAT treats eligible members as one taxable person through a representative member; their company-law and other-tax identities remain separate.
overlaps.dangerousShortcut: Propagating the VAT-group identity to Corporation Tax, CRS, ownership or contracts.
questions: Which bodies were members on the transaction date?
Who was the representative member?
Does a statutory exception stop an intra-group supply being disregarded?
reviewTriggers: Membership or representative member changed.
Overseas establishments or bought-in services are involved.
Joint and several liability matters.

overlaps.label: No new legal person, but a local tax presence
overlaps.meaning: The branch or PE is part of the foreign person, yet its local activity can create and measure a local charge.
overlaps.dangerousShortcut: Treating the PE as a resident subsidiary or treating non-separate as non-taxable.
questions: Which domestic law and treaty definition applies?
What activity, place or agent creates the nexus?
What profit is attributable after the existence question is answered?
reviewTriggers: Remote staff or dependent agents.
A subsidiary also performs parent activity.
Direct-tax PE and VAT fixed-establishment results differ.

overlaps.label: Trust legal title, benefit, control and tax attribution
overlaps.meaning: Trustees can hold legal title, beneficiaries can hold or expect benefit, reporting regimes can name controlling roles, and tax can attribute an item to trustees, beneficiaries or a settlor.
overlaps.dangerousShortcut: Naming one universal owner or taxpayer for the trust.
questions: What type of trust and entitlement exists?
Which income, gain, tax and period are in view?
Which role is being asked about: title, benefit, control, charge or filing?
reviewTriggers: Bare-trust status is uncertain.
Settlor-interest rules may apply.
Classes of beneficiaries, protectors or cross-border residence are present.

overlaps.label: One legal form, different countries' tax classifications
overlaps.meaning: A jurisdiction can treat a body as separate while another looks through it or follows an election. Both classifications can be correct in their own scopes.
overlaps.dangerousShortcut: Forcing one country-wide entity type or treating the mismatch as dirty data.
questions: Which jurisdiction, charge and period does each classification cover?
Was an election made and when did it take effect?
Do anti-hybrid, treaty or reporting rules respond to the mismatch?
reviewTriggers: A foreign entity, election or disregarded status appears.
Payments cross between differently classified entities.
Treaty entitlement or hybrid-mismatch rules may matter.

milestones.title: Partnership law declared and amended
milestones.change: The Partnership Act 1890 put the statutory relationship definition and the Scottish legal-person rule into one Act.
milestones.continuity: Partnership was not invented in 1890, and later tax statutes still decide charge-specific treatment.

milestones.title: UK company residence gained an incorporation rule
milestones.change: The statutory incorporation rule joined the older central-management-and-control doctrine.
milestones.continuity: Management facts and treaty coordination remain relevant; registered office and residence are not synonyms.

milestones.title: VAT Act 1994 consolidated VAT grouping rules
milestones.change: The current statutory framework permits eligible persons to be treated together for VAT through a representative member.
milestones.continuity: Members keep separate legal identities and can retain liability.

milestones.title: US check-the-box classification became applicable
milestones.change: Eligible entities gained default and elective US federal tax classifications that can diverge from legal form.
milestones.continuity: The election does not change the state-law entity or compel another country to follow it.

milestones.title: Parliament created the Great Britain LLP form
milestones.change: The LLP Act 2000 created a body corporate with personality separate from its members for England, Wales and Scotland.
milestones.continuity: Northern Ireland initially followed a separate 2002 Act; tax legislation separately supplies normal partnership treatment when its conditions are met.

milestones.title: Northern Ireland created a separate LLP form
milestones.change: The Northern Ireland Act created an LLP body corporate with personality separate from its members.
milestones.continuity: This separate Act was later ended when the Great Britain LLP enactments were extended to Northern Ireland.

milestones.title: Companies Act 2006 restated the incorporation effect
milestones.change: The current company-law framework states that registration forms the body corporate.
milestones.continuity: Tax, charity, reporting and control overlays remain separate questions.

milestones.title: Parliament provided for Great Britain LLP legislation to extend to Northern Ireland
milestones.change: Companies Act 2006 section 1286 provided for the Great Britain LLP enactments to extend to Northern Ireland and for the separate 2002 Act to cease to have effect.
milestones.continuity: Point-in-time work still needs formation, commencement and transitional facts.

milestones.title: Finance Act 2010 aligned core tax charity definitions
milestones.change: Tax legislation supplied cross-tax definitions of charity, charitable company and charitable trust.
milestones.continuity: The legal form and the conditions of each relief still matter.

milestones.title: BEPS Action 7 strengthened the model PE tests
milestones.change: The OECD final report proposed changes addressing commissionnaire arrangements, preparatory or auxiliary exceptions, fragmentation and contract splitting.
milestones.continuity: A model-standard change does not itself create a UK PE; the actual treaty, domestic law, effective date and facts remain controlling.

milestones.title: FATF strengthened legal-person beneficial-ownership standards
milestones.change: Revised Recommendation 24 strengthened access to adequate, accurate and up-to-date natural-person ownership and control information.
milestones.continuity: Beneficial ownership remains distinct from legal title, tax liability and guilt.

milestones.title: Residence replaced domicile in the reformed personal-tax scope
milestones.change: HMRC states that from 6 April 2025 domicile ceased to be the relevant connecting factor in the changed regime and residence-based rules apply.
milestones.continuity: Domicile remains relevant to historical periods and must not be silently erased.

milestones.title: OECD consolidated the amended CRS
milestones.change: The consolidation brings the original and amended reporting classifications and controlling-person rules together.
milestones.continuity: Domestic adoption and later exchange dates govern actual obligations.

gaps.title: No universal legal-form equivalence
gaps.why: The same translated label can carry different rights and tax treatment. This release does not claim that UK company, partnership or trust forms map one-to-one to foreign forms.
gaps.safeNextStep: Read the foreign governing law, constitutional documents and the applying jurisdiction's classification rule.

gaps.title: No all-tax outcome table
gaps.why: A form-by-tax table would falsely imply that the form alone determines each outcome.
gaps.safeNextStep: Assess the exact charge, item, capacity, jurisdiction and period.

gaps.title: No bilateral-treaty result
gaps.why: The OECD Model explains concepts but actual treaties and protocols differ.
gaps.safeNextStep: Read the current treaty text and domestic implementation for both states.

gaps.title: No natural-person ownership or control graph
gaps.why: Beneficial ownership can be sensitive personal data and this public corpus contains only roles and synthetic examples.
gaps.safeNextStep: Keep verified private records in an approved matter or compliance system with access controls.

gaps.title: No hosted personal classification
gaps.why: This release is a public framework and synthetic interpreter. It accepts no private facts and makes no authority-facing decision.
gaps.safeNextStep: Use the schema locally, retain sources and facts, and obtain qualified review for consequential cases.

gaps.title: No numerical legal confidence
gaps.why: A percentage would hide whether the gap is law, evidence, dates, jurisdiction or contested authority.
gaps.safeNextStep: Report missing facts, competing classifications, source authority and a plain review reason.

gaps.title: Community interest companies not yet modelled
gaps.why: A CIC combines company form with a separate community-interest and asset-lock regime; the current company and charity archetypes do not express that combination.
gaps.safeNextStep: Add CIC legislation, regulator status, company-tax treatment, control and activity-specific examples before classifying one.

gaps.title: Charitable incorporated organisations not yet modelled
gaps.why: A CIO is an incorporated charity form without the same Companies Act identity as a charitable company.
gaps.safeNextStep: Add separate England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland form and tax sources rather than mapping a CIO to a company by name.

gaps.title: Limited partnerships not yet modelled
gaps.why: General partners, limited partners, Scottish legal personality, private-fund rules and registration changes require more than the general-partnership archetypes.
gaps.safeNextStep: Model each territorial form, partner role, charge and effective period from the Limited Partnerships Act and current tax guidance.

gaps.title: Mutuals not yet modelled
gaps.why: Co-operative societies, community benefit societies, friendly societies, building societies and other mutual forms have different governing and tax rules.
gaps.safeNextStep: Split the family by statute and activity before adding legal-form, attribution, reporting and obligation classifications.

gaps.title: Unincorporated associations not yet modelled
gaps.why: An association can lack separate general-law personality while tax and administration still assign duties to officers, trustees or the association name.
gaps.safeNextStep: Add governing-law, Corporation Tax, trust-property and officer-duty sources with separate synthetic subjects.

gaps.title: Statutory bodies not yet modelled
gaps.why: Public corporations, authorities and office-holders derive identity and exemptions from their own enactments rather than one reusable company rule.
gaps.safeNextStep: Model each statutory body's creating instrument, tax provision, public function and filing role separately.

gaps.title: Investment vehicles not yet modelled
gaps.why: REITs, investment trusts, OEICs, unit trusts, limited-partnership funds and other vehicles combine legal form, elections, regulatory status and investor-level tax in different ways.
gaps.safeNextStep: Add vehicle-specific legal, regulatory, tax-attribution, reporting and election sources before publishing classifications.
